# Numerical zero presentation first observation

The small closed project applies eight eighth-turn phases between two
Hadamards on one qubit. Its output bit is last. Exact interference makes
that bit zero. A separate product of four H–T–H preparations gives the
visible `11110` outcome probability `((2 - sqrt(2)) / 4)^4`.

[The original observation](before-run.json) retains the unannotated numerical
text and JSON commands, results and executable identities recorded before
#133's classifier. The first execution showed a positive floating residual
for `00001` around `3.27e-33` and a genuine positive `11110` probability
around `4.60e-4`. The source and manifest in `attempt-01` preserve the bytes
used in that execution. The CLI regression reruns the project and compares
opt-in annotations to the unaltered current numerical distribution.
